-*- Mode: Text; Base: 10 -*-

From ISO 10303-11:2004(E)

========== Chapter 11 Interface spectification ==========

Interfaces come in three types, USE FROM, REFERENCE FROM and implicitly.

USE FROM applies only to ENTITY and TYPE and can be
"chained". I.e. when S2 is USE FROM'd in S1, then any declarations
USE'd into S2 are also visible in S1. REFERECE FROM cannot be
"chained" since you cannot reference an object that was referenced
into a schema.

If a USE FROM has not resources the all TYPE's and ENTITY's are
considered to be interfaced.  That also means that any TYPE's and
ENTITY's which were USE FROM'd into the schema are also visible.


===== USE FROM =====

Only interfaces ENTITY and TYPE.

When a schema is USE FROM'd, TYPE and ENTITY declarations from its USE
FROM's are also included.
